units.text: The `ui-test-junit4` module includes a `ComposeTestRule` and an implementation for Android called `AndroidComposeTestRule`. Through this rule you can set Compose content or access the activity. You construct the rules using factory functions, either `createComposeRule` or, if you need access to an activity, `createAndroidComposeRule`.

units.text: A typical UI test for Compose looks like this:

quotes.quote: A typical UI test for Compose looks like this:

// file: app/src/androidTest/java/com/package/MyComposeTest.kt class MyComposeTest { @get:Rule val composeTestRule = createComposeRule() // use createAndroidComposeRule<YourActivity>() if you need access to // an activity @Test fun myTest() { // Start the app composeTestRule.setContent { MyAppTheme { MainScreen(uiState = fakeUiState, /*...*/) } } composeTestRule.onNodeWithText("Continue").performClick() composeTestRule.onNodeWithText("Welcome").assertIsDisplayed()

units.text: The v2 versions of the Compose testing APIs are now available to improve control over coroutine execution. This update does not duplicate the entire API surface; only the APIs that establish the test environment have been updated.

quotes.quote: are now available to improve control over coroutine execution. This update does not duplicate the entire API surface; only the APIs that establish the test environment have been updated.

units.text: The v1 APIs are deprecated, and it's strongly recommended to migrate to the new APIs.

quotes.quote: The v1 APIs are deprecated, and it's strongly recommended to migrate to the new APIs.

units.text: While the v1 APIs relied on the `UnconfinedTestDispatcher`, the v2 APIs use the `StandardTestDispatcher` by default for the running composition.

quotes.quote: While the v1 APIs relied on the UnconfinedTestDispatcher, the v2 APIs use the StandardTestDispatcher by default for the running composition.

units.text: The deprecated `androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.createComposeRule`, `createAndroidComposeRule` and `createEmptyComposeRule` are replaced by the functions of the same names in `androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.v2`. The deprecated `androidx.compose.ui.test.runComposeUiTest`, `runAndroidComposeUiTest` and `runEmptyComposeUiTest` are replaced by the functions of the same names in `androidx.compose.ui.test.v2`.

units.text: The `runComposeUiTest` API automatically executes your test block within its own `runTest` scope. The test clock is synchronized with the Compose environment, so you no longer need to manage the scheduler manually.

quotes.quote: The runComposeUiTest API automatically executes your test block within its own runTest scope. The test clock is synchronized with the Compose environment, so you no longer need to manage the scheduler manually.

fun testWithCoroutines() = runComposeUiTest { setContent { var status by remember { mutableStateOf("Loading...") } LaunchedEffect(Unit) { delay(1000) status = "Done!" } Text(text = status) } onNodeWithText("Loading...").assertIsDisplayed() mainClock.advanceTimeBy(1000 + 16 /* Frame buffer */) onNodeWithText("Done!").assertIsDisplayed()

units.text: The Robolectric blog post "sharedTest" (2021) shows a pattern called `sharedTest` to share tests between local and instrumentation tests. According to the post, the first thing that `sharedTest` needs is the `AndroidJUnit4` test runner, a test runner that supports both Robolectric and androidx.test.

quotes.quote: This article will show an often overlooked but widely-used pattern called sharedTest to share tests between local and instrumentation tests.
The first thing that sharedTest needs is AndroidJUnit4 test runner. It is a test runner that supports both Robolectric and androidx.test.

units.text: The post says that if `AndroidJUnit4` finds the current running environment has `RobolectricTestRunner`, it delegates tests to Robolectric's `RobolectricTestRunner`; otherwise to androidx.test's `AndroidJUnit4ClassRunner`.

quotes.quote: If it finds current running environment has RobolectricTestRunner, it will delegate tests to Robolectric's RobolectricTestRunner; otherwise to androidx.test's AndroidJUnit4ClassRunner.

units.text: The post says the second thing to enable `sharedTest` is to create a directory called `sharedTest`, at the same directory level with `test` and `androidTest`. The next step it gives is to add the `sharedTest` directory to the source directories of `test` and `androidTest`:

quotes.quote: The second thing to enable sharedTest is to create a directory called sharedTest, at the same directory level with test and androidTest.
The next step we should do is to add sharedTest directory to test's and androidTest's source directory.
// share the unified tests sourceSets { test { java.srcDir 'src/sharedTest/java' } androidTest { java.srcDir 'src/sharedTest/java' } }

units.text: The post's last step is to test it with `./gradlew test` for local tests on Robolectric and `./gradlew connectedCheck` for instrumentation tests on an emulator.

quotes.quote: The last thing is to test it with ./gradlew test for local tests on Robolectric and ./gradlew connectedCheck for instrumentation tests on Emulator.
